Data sources:
- https://data.cityofnewyork.us/Environment/Recycling-Diversion-and-Capture-Rates/gaq9-z3hz/about_data
- https://data.cityofnewyork.us/City-Government/Population-of-the-Limited-English-Proficient-LEP-S/9ji4-nien/about_data
- https://data.cityofnewyork.us/City-Government/Community-Districts/5crt-au7u/about_data 
- https://data.cityofnewyork.us/City-Government/Borough-Boundaries/gthc-hcne/about_data 

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
# load in necessary libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(janitor)
library(sf)
library(showtext)


# import roboto
font_add_google(name = "Roboto", family = "roboto")
```

Diversion file has data from 2016 to 2019. LEP data is from 2024.

```{r}
# read in data
diversion <- read_csv(here("data/Recycling_Diversion_and_Capture_Rates_20261022.csv")) %>% 
  clean_names()
lep <- read_csv(here("data/Population_of_the_Limited_English_Proficient_(LEP)_Speakers_by_Community_District_20261022.csv")) %>% 
  clean_names()
```

Diversion and LEP stores community district IDs differently. Clean accordingly.

```{r}
diversion <- diversion %>% 
  
  # pull the borough
  mutate(borough = case_when(
             str_starts(district, "Q") ~ "4", # Queens
             str_starts(district, "BX") ~ "2", # Bronx
             str_starts(district, "M") ~ "1", # Manhattan
             str_starts(district, "BK") ~ "3", # Brooklyn
             str_starts(district, "SI") ~ "5")) %>%  # Staten Island 
  
  # pull the code
  mutate(code = str_sub(district, -2)) %>% 
    
  # combine borough number and district code to match lep data
  mutate(borough_community_district_code = str_c(borough, code))

# save most recent data, which is 2019
diversion_2019 <- diversion %>% 
  filter(fiscal_year == 2019)
```

```{r}
# sanity check: there should be 59 community districts in each dataset
length(unique(diversion_2019$borough_community_district_code))
length(unique(lep$borough_community_district_code))
```

```{r}
# select necessary columns
## diversion
total_div <- diversion %>% 
  select(fiscal_month_number, borough_community_district_code, diversion_rate_total_total_recycling_total_waste) %>% 
  
  # group by month (take average)
  group_by(borough_community_district_code) %>% 
  
  summarise(avg_diversion = mean(diversion_rate_total_total_recycling_total_waste, na.rm = TRUE))

## lep
lep_clean <- lep %>% 
  select(borough_community_district_code, percent_of_population_that_is_lep, borough) %>% 
  
  # make district code a factor vars
  mutate(borough_community_district_code = as.character(borough_community_district_code))
```

Join LEP and diversion rates data by community district.

```{r}
# join LEP and diversion rates by community district code
div_lep <- total_div %>% 
  left_join(lep_clean, by = "borough_community_district_code")
```

We got the clean data! Let's plot.

```{r}
showtext_auto()

ggplot(data = div_lep, aes(x = percent_of_population_that_is_lep, y = avg_diversion)) +
  geom_point(color = "#fcba03") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "#07543A", linewidth = 0.75) +
  facet_wrap(~borough,
             axes = "all") +
 # stat_ellipse(type = "t") + 
  theme_minimal() +
  xlim(0, 60) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major = element_line(
      linewidth = 0.3),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "#07543A", family = "roboto"))

ggsave(here("plots/scatter.pdf"))

showtext_auto(FALSE)
```

```{r}
ggplot(data = div_lep, aes(x = percent_of_population_that_is_lep, y = avg_diversion, color = borough)) +
  geom_point() 
```


Bar plot comparing diversion for paper, mgp, and leaves

```{r}
# let's rotattteeee (so can group by waste type)
div_long <- diversion %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = capture_rate_paper_total_paper_max_paper:capture_rate_total_total_recycling_leaves_recycling_max_paper_max_mgp_x100,
               names_to = "waste_type",
               values_to = "capture_rate") %>% 
  
  # find average for each type of waste (lumping all community districts together)
  group_by(waste_type) %>% 
  summarise(avg_capture_rate = mean(capture_rate, na.rm = TRUE))

# bar plot!
ggplot(div_long, aes(y = avg_capture_rate, x = waste_type)) +
  geom_col()
```

Mapping diversion rates by community districts

```{r}
geos <- read_sf(here("data/Community_Districts_20261005.geojson"))

# there are a few "joint interest areas" included in this data, representing places like parks 
# we will filter them out

jia_codes <- c(164, 226, 227, 228, 355, 356, 480, 481, 482, 483, 484, 595)

geos_clean <- geos %>% 
  filter(!boro_cd %in% jia_codes)

# keep only boro codes and geos
geos_clean <- geos_clean %>% 
  select(boro_cd, geometry)
```

```{r}
# join diversion data to district geos
geos_div <- total_div %>% 
  left_join(geos_clean, by = c("borough_community_district_code" = "boro_cd")) %>% 
  st_as_sf()
```

```{r}
plot(geos_div)
```

```{r}
# read in borough boundaries, to plot on top
boros <- read_sf(here("data/Borough_Boundaries_20261022.geojson"))

# ensure it is the same crs as community districts
boros <- st_transform(boros, crs = st_crs(geos_div))
```

```{r}
div_map <- ggplot() +
  
  # community districts (plotting by diversion rate)
  geom_sf(data = geos_div, aes(fill = avg_diversion), color = "white") +
  
  # set color palette
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#7cc04a", high = "#07543A") +
  
  labs(fill = " ") + 
  
  # borough outlines
  geom_sf(data = boros, color = "gray75", fill = "transparent", linewidth = 0.6) + 
  
  
  scale_color_discrete(guide = "none") +
  
  theme_void() + 
  
  theme(legend.direction = "horizontal",
        legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.key.width = unit(.7, "cm"),
        legend.key.height = unit(0.3, "cm"))

ggsave(here("plots/map.pdf"), div_map)
```

yearly diversion
```{r}
# read in diversion data
yearly <- read_csv(here("data/dsny yearly diversion.csv")) %>% 
 clean_names()
```
plot as line graph
```{r}
showtext_auto()

ggplot(yearly, aes(x = year, y = diversion_rate, group = 1)) +
  geom_line(color = "#fcba03") +
  labs(x = " ",
       y = " ") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        axis.text = element_text(color = "gray75",  family = "roboto")) +
  ylim(13, 21) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(13, 21),
    breaks = seq(13, 21, by = 2),
    labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(min(yearly$year), max(yearly$year), by = 2)
  )

ggsave("plots/yearly.pdf", width = 8, height = 4, unit = "in")

showtext_auto(FALSE)
```
